title: Journal entries written in the same second silently overwrite each other
description:
`codeyam-editor editor journal` names each entry file from a second-granularity UTC timestamp (`.codeyam/journal/entries/<YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SSZ>.json`) with no collision handling, so two entries written within the same second land on the same path and the second silently replaces the first.

Reproduced while filing two unrelated defect reports back to back:

  journal: wrote entry "Design-round mockups never reach the Mockups tab..." to .codeyam/journal/entries/2026-08-15T19-50-05Z.json
  journal: wrote entry "Preview proxy injects <base href=...>..."        to .codeyam/journal/entries/2026-08-15T19-50-05Z.json

Both commands reported success and exited 0, but only one file exists and it contains only the second entry. The first was lost with no warning, no error, and no indication in the CLI output that anything was overwritten — the reported path is the only clue, and it is easy to miss because the two lines scroll past together.

This is most likely to bite exactly when it hurts most: an agent filing several findings at the end of a session, or a scripted/batched write, will lose all but the last entry of each second. The failure is silent and unrecoverable — the overwritten content is simply gone.

Suggested fix: on collision, either append a disambiguating suffix (`...Z-2.json`), fall back to sub-second precision, or refuse the write with a non-zero exit rather than clobbering. Any of the three is better than a silent overwrite; the suffix keeps the command non-blocking for batch use.

Workaround: re-file the lost entry (a later second yields a fresh filename), and verify after each write that the reported path is distinct from the previous one.

Observed on the puzzle-school-rebuild branch.
